Syncing Philips Hue lights with your TV used to be expensive—just the company's Sync Box 8K costs $385. But several new products are bringing the entry point down to as little as $120.

Also, with a new $40 Wall Light Module, you can now integrate Nanoleaf wall panels into the Philips Hue ecosystem...

Sync Hue lights with your TV

Syncing Philips Hue lights with your TV—whether you're watching movies or gaming—creates a deeply immersive experience.

The company's Sync Box 8K uses the HDMI signal to detect colors on the TV screen, then adjusts all the Hue lights in the room to match in real time. But at nearly $400, it doesn't come cheap; paired with a Gradient Light Strip, the package for the largest TV size tops $650.

The company is now offering two more affordable options:

  • Sync Box 4K, also HDMI-based: $150
  • Play Screen Sync, camera-based: $120

HDMI syncing is more accurate, and the new 4K model saves money by cutting HDMI inputs from four to one. Maximum supported resolution is 4K 60Hz.

Play Screen Sync works with any content, but at the cost of color-matching accuracy. Similar third-party solutions already exist from companies like Govee.

Nanoleaf integration

The Verge has spotted that Philips has partnered with Nanoleaf to release a new Wall Light Module. This $40 little box makes any Nanoleaf product recognizable as a Philips Hue device.

Although Nanoleaf products already support HomeKit, adding Hue compatibility is useful for third-party apps, offering more flexibility for features like animated scenes and music sync.
